compTexts: A rival power has opened an office in this exact block, mid-chase. — New signage, new staff, a courteous but pointed presence blocking the fastest route — and clearly not moving for anyone. — *Wild:* a staked claim-post, freshly driven. *Dungeon:* a new faction checkpoint. *Urban:* the office, as rolled.

The chase startles something that wasn't part of it. — A nest, a hive, a spooked pack animal — a small, real, unaligned hazard joins for exactly one round. — *Wild:* a disturbed hive. *Dungeon:* a nest of vermin. *Urban:* a spooked cart-horse.

Something drops or falls from above. — A branch, loose masonry, a dropped crate from a window — no malice in it, just bad luck at a bad time. — *Wild:* a dead branch lets go. *Dungeon:* loose ceiling debris. *Urban:* a dropped crate from a balcony.

Weather turns, mid-chase. — Rain, wind, dust — visibility and footing both take a hit for the rest of the chase, not just this round. — *Wild:* a sudden squall. *Dungeon:* a ventilation-shaft downdraft. *Urban:* a dust-devil off the rooftops.

The ground gives way underfoot. — A rut, a loose stair, a patch of scree — whoever fails the check stumbles and the gap shifts a half-segment against them. — *Wild:* a rabbit warren collapses underfoot. *Dungeon:* a rotten floor plank. *Urban:* a caved storm-drain grate.

The chase's noise wakes a sleeping household or camp. — Lights come up, voices rise, and for a beat there are more eyes on the street than there were a moment ago. — *Wild:* a hunting camp stirs. *Dungeon:* a barracks room wakes. *Urban:* a tenement's windows light up.

findings.text: Chase A ended AWAY — checking whether the escaped foe persists as a soft recall (digest/codex) per the mission's contract.

moraleTrigger(foe,combat) auto-derivation returned {ok:false,reason:'no-trigger'} for a SOLO foe fight (side-bloodied/bloodied-outnumbered both require foes.length>1 by their own formula — unreachable for a 1-foe skirmish). The DM had to supply p.trigger:'first-blood' by hand, which works, but it means solo-foe fights (a lone lookout, a single guard) have no built-in morale checkpoint the DM doesn't have to invent from scratch each time — a coherence gap next to the multi-foe triggers.

COMBAT-LIFECYCLE §3d ORDERING VIOLATION: for a SOLO foe, foe_morale's flee application calls cmMaybeAutoEnd (§3b) which auto-fires combat_end IMMEDIATELY (all foes are now fled/down) — GS.combat is torn down before the DM's next turn can emit chase_start 'before combat_end' as the doc contracts. Repro isolated: applyEvent(combat_start 1 foe) -> applyEvent(foe_morale, forces flee) leaves GS.combat===null already. chase_start still 'works' by degrading to a generic quarry name (loses the foe's actual name/identity in the ledger line) rather than failing loudly. This is arguably the MOST common real-play trigger for direction-2 chases (one guard/lookout breaks and runs) so this isn't an edge case.
chase_start degraded to the generic quarry name 'the quarry' instead of 'Cartel Lookout' — direct consequence of the §3d race above; the ledger's chase-start line loses the foe's identity.
Encounter C reproduces the SAME §3d race as Encounter B (solo-foe flee auto-tears-down combat before chase_start) — confirms it is deterministic/systemic, not a one-off RNG fluke.
